species.real: A king penguin chick takes so long to raise that a pair manages at most two chicks every three years.
species.name: Oakling

dex.text: A brown, bobbling ball of fluff that stands about in a crowd for most of a year, waiting for its coat to come off. Looks like a small owl wearing a large doormat.
dex.fact: A king penguin chick keeps its thick brown down for around a year, the longest of any penguin; sealers on South Georgia nicknamed the chicks oakum boys.

species.real: King penguins regularly dive deeper than 100 metres for lanternfish, and now and then past 300, all on one breath.
species.name: Kingwalker

dex.text: Stands in tens of thousands on a beach in South Georgia, in what is either a parade or a very long queue for the loo. Moves in a stately waddle and does not hurry for anyone, including the weather.
dex.fact: King penguins do not build nests: each parent balances the single egg on top of its feet, under a warm fold of belly skin, and they take turns.
